solutions.explanation:
Begin with the innermost fraction, which requires \(a\ne1\). For these values,
\[
1+\frac{a}{1-a}
=\frac{1-a+a}{1-a}
=\frac{1}{1-a}.
\]
This quantity is never zero, so the outer division introduces no additional restriction. Its reciprocal is \(1-a\), and therefore
\[
1-\frac{1}{1+\frac{a}{1-a}}
=1-(1-a)=a.
\]
The original expression remains undefined at \(a=1\), even though the simplified expression \(a\) alone is defined there. Thus the simplest form is \(\boxed{a\text{ with }a\ne1}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Simplify from the inside
